title: A Perfect Smoother

citations.claim: Eilers introduced the Whittaker smoother to the analytical chemistry community as a penalized least squares method that balances fidelity to data against roughness of the fitted curve, controlled by a single smoothing parameter lambda.
The Whittaker smoother solves the linear system (I + lambda * D'D)z = y, where D is a difference matrix of order d and lambda controls the trade-off between data fidelity and smoothness.

Eilers showed that incorporating a diagonal weight matrix W into the penalized least squares framework yields the system (W + lambda * D'D)z = Wy, enabling automatic handling of missing data and asymmetric fitting.

The Whittaker smoother can be implemented efficiently using sparse matrices, smoothing a series of 100,000 observations in a few seconds with linear computational complexity in the number of data points.
The difference order d in the Whittaker smoother determines the limiting polynomial behavior under strong smoothing: d=1 yields a constant, d=2 a straight line, and d=3 a parabola.
The Whittaker smoother provides continuous control over smoothness with a single parameter lambda, unlike the Savitzky-Golay filter whose smoothness is controlled by a discrete window size.
Eilers demonstrated that leave-one-out cross-validation can be performed efficiently for the Whittaker smoother using the hat matrix diagonal, enabling automatic selection of the smoothing parameter.

do_not_claim: Eilers proposed the Whittaker smoother for baseline correction (he proposed it for general smoothing, not baseline correction specifically)
Eilers introduced asymmetric weights for baseline estimation (the asymmetric least squares extension came in a later 2005 unpublished report by Eilers and Boelens)
The Whittaker smoother was invented by Eilers (it was originally proposed by Whittaker in 1923; Eilers modernized it)
